<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The `makepkg --printsrcinfo` command only sources/parses the PKGBUILD's top-level scope and does not execute any function bodies. Examining the global scope of this PKGBUILD, every line is a standard variable assignment or array definition: `pkgname`, `pkgver`, `pkgrel`, `pkgdesc`, `arch`, `url`, `license`, `depends`, `optdepends`, `provides`, `conflicts`, `options`, `source`, and `sha256sums`. There are no command substitutions (`$(...)` or backticks), no `eval`, no `exec`, no network calls, and no file operations at top level.

The `source=` array uses simple string interpolation with `$url` and `$pkgver`, both of which are already-defined plain variables. This only constructs a URL string for a download to the project's own upstream GitHub releases host (`github.com/kjmcnamara1/cecilia`); no code is executed and no network activity occurs during sourcing. The `package()` function, which contains a local script invocation (`linux/stage.sh`), is defined but never executed by `--printsrcinfo` — it is out of scope for this gate and will be reviewed separately.

No obfuscation, encoding, or unusual constructs are present. This is a standard prebuilt-binary package layout consistent with normal AUR packaging practices. The checksum is provided (not SKIP) and points to a verifiable upstream artifact.

</details>
<evidence>

</evidence>
<summary>
All top-level scope is benign variable assignments; no executable code runs during --printsrcinfo.
</summary>
</security_assessment>
